title: PipeTier indexes fixed-size tier arrays without a local bounds check in RoutingRebuild/BundlesRebuild
evidence: PP_Routing.h:168: const int32_t Nd = Dist[Cur] + kTierCost[T.PipeTier[Pi]];  PP_Routing.h:207: const int32_t C = kTierCost[T.PipeTier[Pi]];  PP_Bundles.h:103: B.BundleCap.push_back(static_cast<uint32_t>(kTierCapacity[T.PipeTier[Pi]]));  PP_Bundles.h:109: B.BundleCap[Found] += static_cast<uint32_t>(kTierCapacity[T.PipeTier[Pi]]);  (arrays: PP_Balance.h:38,42: inline constexpr int32_t kTierCost[TIER_COUNT] = {20, 10, 5}; inline constexpr int32_t kTierCapacity[TIER_COUNT] = {10, 15, 40}; with TIER_COUNT = 3, while PipeTier is uint16_t and is serialized: PP_Sim.h:207: PutU16(State.Topology.PipeTier[I]);)
detail: Today unreachable: every write goes through ValidateDraw's 'if (Tier >= TIER_COUNT) return UnknownTier;' and no deserializer exists. But v2 wire format persists tier as u16 and readers are anticipated; a future loader that skips revalidation turns a corrupt save into an OOB constexpr read feeding routing math.
recommended_fix: In the future deserializer, re-validate tier < TIER_COUNT (reject corrupt saves); optionally add a defensive bounds check or clamp at the RoutingRebuild/BundlesRebuild index sites.
